scope: P01 onward, including future added pages
purpose: Separate high-saliency authored display art, variable native copy, shared publication furniture, photos and page-specific ornaments so V30 stays editorially rich without rasterizing everything or flattening the publication into generic Figma UI.
authorityPrinciple: Latest owner feedback and item/page authority win. Do not classify by text-vs-image ideology. Classify by editorial role, mutability, saliency, reuse scope and actual implementation need.

evidence: V10 P02 recipe explicitly expected TITLE_PROFILE_* as a major asset role.
V10 Anti-AI authority states that strong Rurubu display typography has a silhouette and hero display art may be generated/composed when that materially improves quality.
V10 also states that motifs should be reused with variation rather than exact cloning.

The project-wide AI-Figma Hybrid Authoring Policy correctly protects variable semantic copy as native, but its old examples of names/headings must not be interpreted as an unconditional ban on item-authorized locked display art.
Earlier Drive/V20 production includes generated P02 editorial parts such as V20_P02_PROFILE_BADGE_GEN_A.png.
historicalReconciliation.resolution: Variable/long/TBD/factual copy remains native by default. Short locked high-saliency display text may become GENERATED_DISPLAY_ASSET only when current item/page authority explicitly classifies it that way and the canonical exact string remains recorded outside the raster asset.
historicalReconciliation.hardReject: Do not let an older generic native-text default override a newer explicit item/page display-art classification.

GENERATED_DISPLAY_ASSET.definition: Short locked high-saliency editorial display art whose lettering, vessel, outline, shadow and local accents materially behave as one authored object.
examples: locked name labels where lettering treatment is part of the page identity
rules: exact visible wording must be owner-approved/locked before generation
canonical source text remains recorded in authority/metadata even when visible lettering is raster/vector art
use only when authored display treatment materially improves the Rurubu/V30 result versus native reconstruction
QA spelling, silhouette, alpha/material integrity and A5 readability
do not use this role for long, personal, TBD or frequently changing copy

NATIVE_TEXT.definition: Copy that benefits from continued editability or is long, variable, TBD, factual/personal, frequently changing, or not explicitly approved for baked display-art treatment.
NATIVE_TEXT.rule: Native text is not the default merely because an element contains text; mutability and editorial role decide first.

SHARED_PUBLICATION_COMPONENT.definition: Cross-page recurring publication furniture with one master visual system and controlled variable content.
SHARED_PUBLICATION_COMPONENT.rule: Design once as a master component/system, then instantiate across pages. Do not independently redraw or regenerate one version per page.

PAGE_SPECIFIC_ORNAMENT.definition: Local decorative/editorial art whose composition belongs to one page position and narrative job.
PAGE_SPECIFIC_ORNAMENT.rule: May belong to a global ornament family, but final composition is page-specific unless repetition is intentionally declared.

PHOTO.definition: Replaceable real or clean standalone proxy photography.

decisionOrder: Does it repeat across pages with only controlled variable content? -> SHARED_PUBLICATION_COMPONENT
Is it page-specific decoration with no essential locked display copy? -> PAGE_SPECIFIC_ORNAMENT
Is it long/variable/TBD/personal/frequently changing or not copy-locked? -> NATIVE_TEXT
Is it short, locked, high-saliency editorial lettering whose authored treatment materially defines the page and is explicitly item/page-authorized? -> GENERATED_DISPLAY_ASSET

liveImplementationContract.principle: A manifest role is not a PASS until the live Figma implementation actually matches it.
checks: GENERATED_DISPLAY_ASSET declared -> verify the live high-saliency role is actually installed as the approved authored asset rather than leftover generic native reconstruction
NATIVE_TEXT declared -> verify wording remains separately controllable and is not silently baked into unrelated art
SHARED_PUBLICATION_COMPONENT declared -> verify actual shared-master provenance, not just similar naming or visual resemblance
PAGE_SPECIFIC_ORNAMENT declared -> verify its active source is page-specific or intentionally declared recurring, not an undeclared exact carry-over
PHOTO declared -> verify stable replaceable photo role/mask rather than page screenshot or decorated proxy
hardRejects: marking a shared component PASS because the manifest says shared while Figma contains unrelated page-specific constructions
marking generated display art PASS while the live page still uses the rejected native placeholder treatment
marking page-specific ornament PASS without checking active source provenance

sharedPageBadgeSystem.designRule: PAGE 01, PAGE 02 and later page badges are one publication component, not separate page designs.

recommendedArchitecture.master: one authored/generated decorative badge shell derived from the V30/Rurubu visual language, installed as one Figma component
recommendedArchitecture.variable: page number is a component text/property variable; PAGE label may remain fixed within the component
recommendedArchitecture.instances: P01 onward use instances/variants of the same master
recommendedArchitecture.reason: This preserves exact cross-page design while avoiding independently generated page PNGs and scales naturally to P09+.

implementationProof: inspect actual Figma component/instance relationship or approved master-source relationship
verify shell, stroke, typography behavior, icon treatment and scale are inherited from one master
verify only declared variable content changes between pages
do not accept semantic naming alone as proof
sharedPageBadgeSystem.currentCalibration: P01 PAGE 01 is a visual calibration source, but must migrate into the shared master rather than remain an isolated P01-only raster beside unrelated later badges.
hardRejects: P01 raster badge beside a separately designed P02 ellipse badge
same semantic PAGE furniture drifting in stroke, typography, backing, icon or scale across pages
claiming SHARED_PUBLICATION_COMPONENT_PASS without live master/instance provenance

sharedComponentInventoryPolicy.principle: Identify recurring publication furniture globally before per-page completion, but promote something to SHARED_PUBLICATION_COMPONENT only after its repeated semantic job is confirmed.
sharedComponentInventoryPolicy.futurePageRule: P09+ first consumes existing confirmed shared masters. New shared furniture is added only when recurrence is real, not predicted from convenience.

displayFamilyProduction.rule: Related display assets should be designed/calibrated as a small family or batch when they share one semantic system, then installed independently where composition requires.
examples: title plus subtitle/ribbon treatment when they form one header ecology
displayFamilyProduction.antiPattern: Do not generate a large unrelated display-asset library before page context is known.

gates.DISPLAY_ROLE_CLASSIFICATION_PASS: All material visible elements are classified by editorial role, mutability and saliency rather than text-vs-image alone.
gates.LIVE_ROLE_IMPLEMENTATION_PASS: The live Figma node/source implementation matches the declared role.
gates.DISPLAY_ART_QUALITY_PASS: Generated display assets have publication-grade authored lettering/vessels and do not look like generic Figma text effects.
gates.SHARED_PUBLICATION_COMPONENT_PASS: Shared furniture is implemented from one verifiable master and visually consistent across applicable pages.
gates.COPY_LOCK_PASS: Any generated visible wording is exact, approved and recorded canonically outside the asset.
gates.TRUE_ALPHA_PREFLIGHT_PASS: Floating generated display art follows the current true-alpha generation policy.

futurePageRule: P09+ inherits confirmed shared component masters automatically and classifies new high-saliency display art using the same decision order. Do not create a new visual system merely because a new page is added.
